idiom_name: hand-written row<->object mapper functions over node-postgres (pg)
implementation_notes: Node has no persistence layer in the runtime: pg hands back plain row objects in result.rows, so the mapper is a pair of functions per aggregate (rowToCustomer(row) and saveCustomer(client, customer)) plus a repository object that owns the pool. Nothing in the language knows the schema, which makes the mapping entirely explicit and is exactly the Data Mapper structure without metadata. The ecosystem mostly implements the opposite pattern - Sequelize and Mongoose are Active Record - while TypeORM offers a repository-based DataMapper mode and Prisma generates a typed client instead of mapping your domain classes.
pitfalls: pg returns numeric, bigint and decimal columns as strings to preserve precision; convert them in the mapper, not at call sites, or arithmetic silently becomes concatenation.
A pool.query issued inside a transaction escapes it because it checks out a different connection - write mappers must take the checked-out client.
Column typos yield undefined rather than an error; validate the row shape inside the mapper instead of letting undefined reach the domain object.
There is no identity map: loading the same row twice gives two objects, so keep a per-request cache when the domain compares object identity.
